topic: Using Smart Pointers for Automatic Resource Management
explanation: In modern C++, smart pointers are used to manage dynamic memory automatically, ensuring proper resource deallocation and preventing memory leaks. They encapsulate raw pointers and provide ownership semantics, making resource management safer and more expressive. This approach leverages RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) principles, which tie resource lifetime to object lifetime, simplifying exception-safe code.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of std::unique_ptr to manage a dynamically allocated Widget object. It shows how ownership can be transferred using std::move, and emphasizes that the resource (Widget) is automatically destroyed when the smart pointer goes out of scope. This exemplifies modern C++ resource management practices, reducing the risk of memory leaks and dangling pointers.
